workflows.name: Reservation lifecycle
workflows.trigger: Guest requests one or more rooms for a date range
steps: Search availability for dates and occupancy
Select room type(s) and rate plan
Confirm and optionally pay deposit
Check in on arrival
Check out and settle folio
Complete, or cancel/no-show before arrival

workflows.name: Housekeeping task lifecycle
workflows.trigger: A room needs turnover after checkout or on a cleaning schedule
steps: Room marked dirty on checkout
Housekeeper assigned and cleans
Mark clean
Supervisor inspects and approves

workflows.name: Night audit workflow
workflows.trigger: End of the property's business day
steps: Post room charges for the day to open folios
Reconcile payments taken against the day's transactions
Resolve no-shows and auto-cancellations
Roll the business date forward

workflows.name: Channel ARI sync workflow
workflows.trigger: Availability, rate, or inventory changes on the property side, or a reservation arrives from a channel
steps: Push updated availability/rate/inventory (ARI) to connected channels
Receive reservation from channel
Map channel room type/rate to internal room type/rate plan
Create internal reservation

provenance.notes: State machine models the channel connection's own health (connected/error/disconnected), evidenced by QloApps's channel-manager connection status; the ARI push/pull exchange itself is a stateless sync operation, not modeled as a separate state machine.

workflows.name: Folio and billing workflow
workflows.trigger: A charge is incurred during a stay, or the guest checks out
steps: Post room/incidental charges to the open folio
Apply any deposit already collected
Settle remaining balance at checkout
Close the folio

provenance.notes: Reasoned inference; neither implementation has a distinct folio entity separate from a single order/invoice.

workflows.name: Property and room inventory setup
workflows.trigger: A property manager onboards a new property or expands its room inventory
steps: Create the property record (name, address, default currency, policies)
Define room types with capacity and default rate
Tag amenities on the property and/or its room types
Add individual physical rooms under each room type
Optionally link two or more rooms as connecting/adjoining

provenance.notes: Both implementations model this same property -> room type -> room hierarchy with amenities attached at the room-type/property level; a setup/configuration flow, not a stateful process.

workflows.name: Rate and restriction management
workflows.trigger: A revenue manager prices a room type for a future date range
steps: Create or edit a rate plan for a room type and date range
Attach restrictions: minimum/maximum length of stay, closed-to-arrival/departure, blackout dates
Optionally apply a demand-based (dynamic/yield) adjustment on top of the base rate
Activate the rate plan
Push the updated rate to connected distribution channels

provenance.notes: Rate-plan creation and min/max-stay restrictions are corroborated by three implementations; the demand-based dynamic-pricing step is a reasoned extension (see hospitality.dynamic_pricing's own low confidence) — no implementation inspected computes rates from demand.

workflows.name: Cancellation and no-show handling
workflows.trigger: A guest cancels a reservation, or the property marks a reservation as a no-show after its cancellation cutoff
steps: Guest or staff initiates a cancellation, or staff flags a no-show past the grace period
Look up the cancellation policy that applies to the reservation's rate plan or property
Calculate the refund/penalty from the policy's cutoff-hours and charge basis (nights, percentage, or fixed amount)
Apply the calculated charge or refund against the collected deposit, or post it to the folio
Update the reservation status to cancelled or no_show

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations model cutoff-based cancellation charges (QloApps's refund rules class; woopms's Policy/PolicyRule with hours_before and charge_based_on). Reuses the reservation entity's own cancelled/no_show states (defined in reservation_lifecycle) rather than redefining them here.

workflows.name: Add-on service upsell
workflows.trigger: A guest wants to add a purchasable extra to their stay, at booking or at check-in
steps: Browse available add-on services for the property
Select and attach one or more add-ons to the reservation
Post the add-on charge to the folio
Guest receives an updated total

provenance.notes: QloApps's ServiceProduct classes attach add-ons directly to a booking; Frappe Hospitality instead bundles extras into a priced Hotel Room Package — two different modeling approaches to the same underlying capability.

workflows.name: Cross-property oversight
workflows.trigger: An operator manages more than one property from a single account
steps: Switch between properties in the admin console
View consolidated occupancy and revenue across properties
Apply a rate or policy change to a subset of properties

provenance.notes: QloApps's HotelBranchInformation explicitly models multiple branches under one account; Frappe's Hotel Settings is only company-scoped (a weaker signal).

workflows.name: Post-stay review and loyalty
steps: System sends a post-stay review invitation
Guest submits a rating/review, optionally across categories
The completed stay is credited toward the guest's loyalty tier
If the guest's loyalty tier changes, the guest profile is updated and the guest is notified

provenance.notes: QloApps's qlohotelreview module evidences post-stay reviews; GuestHub's LoyaltyTier enum and UserLoyaltyTierChanged event evidence tier progression as a genuinely stateful part of the guest profile. The tier-recalculation trigger (e.g. stay count/spend thresholds) is reasoned, not evidenced by either implementation.

workflows.name: Room maintenance and out-of-order handling
workflows.trigger: A room is found to be damaged, needs repair, or is intentionally taken offline
steps: Mark the room out_of_order (or temporarily_inactive) with a reason
Room is excluded from availability/inventory while in that state
Maintenance/engineering resolves the issue
Room is marked active and returned to sellable inventory

provenance.notes: Room status values (active/inactive/temporarily_inactive/out_of_order) are already modeled in both implementations; this workflow is the process that drives those transitions, which neither implementation ties to a distinct work-order/ticket entity.
